title: About Jr_AstroCamp & Team Mysterio
reply:
**Jr_AstroCamp: Beyond Earth** (built by **Team Mysterio** for the **NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026**) is an interactive aerospace flight simulator and multi-format STEM learning platform.

Here is what you can explore on this website:
• **Mission Control (`#mission`)**: Command a 30-Sol Moon (Shackleton Crater) or Mars (Jezero Crater) outpost balancing Oxygen, Power, Water, Food, and Radiation.
• **76-Mission Campaign (`#campaign`)**: Fly 76 authentic NASA missions from Project Mercury and Apollo 11 to Artemis III, Perseverance, and James Webb.
• **Simulators Hub (`#simulators`)**: Hands-on 3D & 2D simulators including Rocket Launch, Orbital Docking, Lunar Landing, Mars EDL, Rover Exploration, Black Hole Physics, and 3D Spacesuits.
• **Learning Hub (`#learning`)**: 8-issue STEM Graphic Novel Comics, Audio & Video Lessons, Handwritten Cadet Notebooks, Flashcards, and Quizzes.
• **Astronaut Academy (`#academy`)**: Upgrade NASA training facilities (NBL Pool, 20G Centrifuge), inspect 3D spacecraft, and unlock real astronaut characters.
• **Teacher Hub (`#teacher`)**: NGSS-aligned classroom gradebook, student analytics, and printable Flight Certificates.

title: How to Play & Win the Outpost Simulation
reply:
**How to Play the Outpost Survival Simulation:**

1. **Pick Your Destination & Tier**: Choose the **Moon (Shackleton Crater)** or **Mars (Jezero Crater)** and select one of 5 difficulty tiers (*Explorer, Cadet, Engineer, Scientist, Commander*).
2. **Spend Build Points (BP)**: Use your starting BP in the Outpost Construction panel to build Solar Arrays, Kilopower Reactors, Hydroponic Greenhouses, or Regolith Shielding.
3. **Survive 30 Sols**: Each Sol presents a real NASA telemetry event (solar storms, moonquakes, dust storms, or ECLSS leaks). Compare the resource deltas (`Power`, `Oxygen`, `Water`, `Food`, `Radiation`, `Science`) before picking an option.
4. **Victory Condition**: Keep **Oxygen, Power, Water, and Crew Health above 0%** through Sol 30 while completing your primary science objectives!

title: Simulators Hub & 3D Flight Trainers
reply:
**Simulators Hub (`#simulators`)** gives you direct hands-on control of 9 interactive aerospace trainers:

1. **Rocket Launch & Staging**: Manage throttle, Max-Q aerodynamic stress, and two-stage booster separation.
2. **Orbital Rendezvous & Docking**: Pulse RCS translation thrusters to dock with the ISS/Agena at $< 0.1\text{ m/s}$.
3. **Apollo Lunar Landing**: Pilot the Lunar Module over boulder fields before descent propellant runs dry.
4. **Mars EDL (7 Minutes of Terror)**: Survive hypersonic entry ($1,300^\circ\text{C}$), parachute deploy, and Sky Crane touchdown.
5. **Planetary Rover Exploration**: Drive Perseverance across Jezero Crater to drill core samples.
6. **Deep Space Telescope (JWST)**: Align 18 gold hexagonal mirror segments at the L2 Lagrange point.
7. **Black Hole Gravitational Lab**: Visualize event horizons, photon spheres, and relativistic accretion disks.
8. **3D Spacesuit & Spacecraft Viewer**: Inspect NASA's xEMU, ACES Pumpkin Suit, Apollo LM, and Perseverance in 360° 3D.
9. **Hardcore Survival & Moonbase Alpha**: Repair life-support loops under real-time solar storm and moonquake emergencies.

title: Surviving the 14-Day Lunar Night & Kilopower KRUSTY
reply:
On the Moon, a single night lasts **~14 Earth days (354 hours)** with temperatures plunging to **-208°C (-342°F)** in polar craters. During this cryogenic blackout, solar panels generate **0 kW**.

**How NASA Survives Lunar Night:**
1. **Kilopower KRUSTY Fission Reactor**: Uses an enriched Uranium-235 core with passive sodium heat pipes and Stirling engines to output a continuous **10 kWe** day and night for 10+ years.
2. **Regolith Thermal Mass**: Sintered lunar soil vaults retain daytime heat.
3. **ECLSS Load Shedding**: Non-essential science loads are throttled down so battery reserves keep habitat life-support heaters above freezing.

title: MOXIE: Making Breathable Oxygen on Mars
reply:
**MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment)** aboard the Perseverance rover generates breathable $\text{O}_2$ directly from the thin Martian atmosphere (which is 95.3% $\text{CO}_2$).

Using **Solid Oxide Electrolysis** at $\sim 800^\circ\text{C}$:
$$2\text{CO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO} + \text{O}_2$$
• MOXIE produces up to **10–12 grams** of 99.6% pure oxygen per hour.
• A human astronaut consumes **$0.84\text{ kg } \text{O}_2\text{/day}$** (~35 g/hour), proving future Mars crews can manufacture both breathing air and liquid oxygen rocket propellant locally instead of hauling it from Earth!
citations: NASA JPL Mars 2020 MOXIE Technical Briefing

title: 7 Minutes of Terror: Mars Entry, Descent & Landing (EDL)
reply:
The **"7 Minutes of Terror"** is the autonomous Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) sequence on Mars. Because radio signals take 7 to 14 minutes one-way between Earth and Mars, the spacecraft must land **100% autonomously**:

1. **Hypersonic Entry**: Hits the atmosphere at $\sim 20,000\text{ km/h}$ ($12,500\text{ mph}$). The aeroshell heat shield withstands **$1,300^\circ\text{C}$** peak heating.
2. **Supersonic Parachute**: Deploys at Mach 1.7 to bleed off 90% of remaining kinetic energy in Mars' thin $610\text{ Pa}$ air.
3. **Terrain-Relative Navigation (TRN)**: Onboard cameras map craters and boulders in real time to pick a safe landing zone.
4. **Sky Crane Maneuver**: Descent hydrazine thrusters hover 20 meters above the ground and lower the rover on nylon bridles until wheel touchdown.
citations: NASA JPL EDL Autonomous Flight Log

title: ECLSS Closed-Loop Water & Air Stoichiometry
reply:
Under the **NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD TP-2015-218570)**, each astronaut requires per day:
• **Oxygen ($\text{O}_2$)**: $0.84\text{ kg/day}$ (exhaling $1.00\text{ kg } \text{CO}_2\text{/day}$)
• **Potable Water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$)**: $2.50\text{–}3.00\text{ L/day}$ (drinking, food prep & hygiene)
• **Food Biomass**: $0.62\text{ kg dry food/day}$ ($\sim 2,500\text{–}3,000\text{ kcal}$)

**How ECLSS Closes the Loop:**
1. **Urine Processor Assembly (UPA)** & **Water Processor Assembly (WPA)**: Recover **98%** of cabin moisture from sweat and urine.
2. **Sabatier Reactor ($400^\circ\text{C}$ nickel/ruthenium catalyst)**:
$$\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
3. **Oxygen Generation Assembly (OGA)**: Electrolyzes that recovered water ($2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2$) back into breathable air!

title: Quindar Tones & the Deep Space Network (DSN)
reply:
**Quindar Tones** are the iconic dual-frequency beeps heard on Apollo and Shuttle voice loops:
• **Intro Tone ($2,525\text{ Hz}$ for $250\text{ ms}$)**: Triggered remote ground transmitters when CapCom pressed Push-To-Talk (PTT).
• **Outro Tone ($2,475\text{ Hz}$ for $250\text{ ms}$)**: Keyed off the remote transmitter when CapCom released PTT.

Today, NASA communicates across the solar system using the **Deep Space Network (DSN)**—three giant **70-meter parabolic dishes** spaced $120^\circ$ apart around Earth in **Goldstone (California), Madrid (Spain), and Canberra (Australia)** so a spacecraft never loses line-of-sight as Earth rotates!
citations: NASA JPL Deep Space Network Monograph

title: Orbital Velocity, Microgravity & Docking
reply:
**Orbital Mechanics & Rendezvous:**
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Velocity**: At $\sim 400\text{ km}$ altitude, a spacecraft must travel at:
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}} \approx 7.8\text{ km/s} \quad (28,000\text{ km/h})$$
Astronauts float in **microgravity** not because gravity is absent (gravity at the ISS is still ~90% of Earth's surface!), but because the station is in continuous sideways freefall around Earth's curve.
• **Earth Escape Velocity**: $11.2\text{ km/s}$ ($40,320\text{ km/h}$) to break free for the Moon or Mars.
• **Orbital Docking Rules**: Never fire main engines near the target. Use short **RCS (Reaction Control System)** pulses, align pitch/yaw crosshairs, and keep closing speed below **$0.1\text{ m/s}$** at contact.

title: Black Holes, Event Horizons & Time Dilation
reply:
**Black Hole Astrophysics (Black Hole Simulator):**
• **Event Horizon (Schwarzschild Radius)**: The boundary where escape velocity equals the speed of light ($c$):
$$R_s = \frac{2GM}{c^2}$$
• **Photon Sphere ($1.5\,R_s$)**: Gravity is so intense that light photons orbit the black hole in a ring, creating the relativistic gravitational lensing halo.
• **Gravitational Time Dilation**: Under Einstein's General Relativity, clocks closer to a massive gravity well tick slower relative to distant observers.
• **Tidal Forces (Spaghettification)**: Extreme gravity gradients stretch infalling matter vertically and compress it horizontally.
citations: NASA Goddard Black Hole Astrophysics Guide
Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) M87* & Sgr A* Papers

title: NASA Spacesuits: EMU, xEMU & ACES
reply:
**Why Astronauts Need Pressurized Spacesuits:**
Above $19\text{ km}$ altitude (**the Armstrong Limit**), atmospheric pressure drops so low ($< 6.3\text{ kPa}$) that water and human saliva boil at normal body temperature ($37^\circ\text{C}$).

• **ACES ("Pumpkin Suit")**: High-visibility orange launch/entry pressure suit with anti-G bladders and emergency parachutes.
• **EMU / Artemis xEMU**: 14-layer miniature personal spacecraft pressurized to **$29.6\text{ kPa}$ ($4.3\text{ psi}$) pure $\text{O}_2$**. Includes a **Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG)** weaving 90 meters of water tubing against the skin, a gold-coated UV visor, Kevlar micrometeoroid weave, and an 8-hour **PLSS** life-support backpack.
citations: NASA Extravehicular Mobility Unit (EMU) Reference Manual
